title: Polynomial time for the padded verifier
statement: Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $V$ be a language of finite binary strings belonging to $\mathrm{P}$. The language of strings that decode as a pair $(x',u)$, with $x'$ decoding as $(x,p)$, such that $p$ is the all-ones string of length $C\cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$, $|u|=C\cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$, and the concatenation $xu$ belongs to $V$, belongs to $\mathrm{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language over the binary alphabet
replaced: For all natural numbers $C, c$ and every language $V$ in $\mathrm{P}$, the paired verifier language for $C$, $c$ and $V$, which checks both pair decodings, the exact all-ones pad of length $C\cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$, the exact witness length, and membership of the assembled word in $V$, belongs to $\mathrm{P}$.
